topics: Combinations ⁿCᵣ (selections where order does not matter)
Restrictions: items grouped together or separated

body.en: Combinatorial principles governing selections, orderings, and arrangements with constraints. A crucial foundation for probability, discrete mathematics, and advanced statistics.

value.en: Treat grouped items as 1 single block, then multiply by internal block arrangements.
Place unrestricted items first, then insert restricted items into spaces (gaps).

body.en:
A group of 4 boys and 3 girls are to sit in a row of 7 chairs. Find the number of possible arrangements if:
(a) All 3 girls must sit together.
(b) No two girls may sit next to each other.

Solution:
(a) Girls together: Treat the 3 girls as 1 composite block \( G \). We now have 4 boys + 1 block = 5 entities to arrange: \( 5! = 120 \). Within the block, the 3 girls can be arranged in \( 3! = 6 \) ways.
Total arrangements = \( 5! \times 3! = 120 \times 6 = 720 \).

(b) No two girls adjacent: First arrange the 4 boys in a row: \( 4! = 24 \) ways.
This creates 5 available gaps (including ends): \( _ B _ B _ B _ B _ \).
We must choose 3 of these 5 gaps for the 3 girls and arrange them: \( {}^5P_3 = 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60 \).
Total arrangements = \( 4! \times {}^5P_3 = 24 \times 60 = 1,440 \).
Answer: (a) 720, (b) 1,440.
